results.evidence: An independent ascent account confirms the line: cross Swamp Creek on a log near 3,600 ft, turn uphill at 4,000 ft into the broad basin below Lyall, aim for the 7,300 ft notch on the southwest ridge, pass the white vertical rock strip, then an exposed Class 3 gully with stacked boulders for the last ~200 ft. Trail data puts Swamp Creek Camp about 8 mi from High Bridge at ~2,800 ft. The only Holden-side report found (Black Tower/Sable Ridge via Hilgard Pass) did not climb Lyall, and no summer ascent of Lyall from Holden turned up. Itinerary numbers (miles/gain per day) were left as stored; they were not settled from sources.

expect.name: High Bridge (Stehekin Valley Road)
expect.note: No road access; reached only by Lady of the Lake passenger ferry from Chelan (~40 mi uplake) to the Lucerne dock, then the Holden Village shuttle (FS Rd 8301, ~11 mi) to Holden, from where trails up Railroad/Tenmile/Company Creek lead to the Tenmile Pass/Hilgard Pass basins used to climb Lyall.

expect.name: Avalanche chute crossings
expect.note: Trail crosses several open, south-facing avalanche chutes on dry terrain; tread can be faint and brushy through slide alder after big snow years.

expect.name: Holden Lake
expect.note: Glacial basin lake with established camping and reliable water; Bonanza Mountain's Mary Green Glacier is visible across the valley — good base camp for the summit push.

expect.name: Basin below Holden Pass
expect.note: Leave the trail here and head off-trail cross-country up open basins toward Holden Pass, the jumping-off point for the south-facing talus/heather slopes to Lyall's summit.

value.name: High Bridge (Stehekin Valley Road)
value.note: No road access: reach Stehekin by the passenger ferry or a floatplane up Lake Chelan, then ride the valley shuttle to the bridge at the road end. The crest trail heads south from here up Agnes Creek toward Swamp Creek, the way in to Lyall's west basin.

expect.cal: Entiat/Glacier Peak Wilderness approach trails typically aren't reliably snow-free until mid-to-late July and can hold lingering blowdown from spring runoff; a late-July through September window is safest.

days.note: A long trail approach through remote Entiat/Glacier Peak Wilderness backcountry, gaining the basin below the peak's south slopes. Expect a mix of maintained and lightly-traveled tread with possible stream crossings and blowdown; most parties camp near treeline to shorten the summit day.

Start early to be off the exposed ground before afternoon storms build.

results.resolution: keep as the Southeast Ridge (no split); rewrite beta only, which was copied from the Northwest Arete and West Ridge descriptions
results.summary: No separate 'East Ridge' climb on Argonaut is documented, so there is nothing to split out and the page stays the Southeast Ridge. Only its route description was replaced, because it had been copied from two other routes on the peak.
results.evidence: The peak's route list names nine lines and no 'East Ridge' route. It gives the Southeast Ridge as II 5.6, 8 pitches to the southeast spire, with two single or one double-rope rappel into the notch. A second route page confirms II 5.6 by the SE spire (false summit) on to the highest point, with blocky, lichen-covered lower pitches, and says the Colchuck Col approach beats the Ingalls Creek bushwhack. The earlier agent's two 'Southeast Ridge' and 'East Ridge' route-page links are for Mount Daniel and Wolfs Head (Wyoming), not Argonaut. The row's beta sentence 'blocky, generally solid but not sustained Class 4 to 5.6 climbing' is word-for-word the Northwest Arete ascent description. 'East faces of towers easier than the west, so you won't cliff out near the crest' is a note about the West Ridge traverse. The 'east ridge to the Argonaut-Colchuck col' appears only as the Northwest Arete's four-rappel descent. Rebuilding the approach, the six-row pitch_detail, descent_text and rappel_detail for the Southeast Ridge needs a full route description that could not be found; those fields are left and flagged.

ops.find: From Colchuck Col, ascend the east ridge featuring blocky, generally solid but not sustained Class 4 to 5.6 climbing. The east faces of towers are typically easier than west sides, making cliff-out less likely if staying near the crest. Multiple pitch sections with good protection opportunities.
ops.replace: Climbs the southeast ridge in about eight pitches up to 5.6 to the southeast spire, a false summit and the lowest of Argonaut's three summits, then carries on to the true summit on the west spire. The lower pitches are blocky and awkward, carry a lot of lichen and are somewhat hard to protect. The line includes two single-rope rappels, or one double-rope rappel, into the notch. The main summit needs a short, non-exposed Class 4 move to its highest block after Class 3 ridge traversing. The Colchuck Col side is the better way to the base; the Ingalls Creek side means a long, strenuous bushwhack.

pin_followups: Not changed, needs a full Southeast Ridge description: approach ('6 pitches' from a notch west of a lone gendarme reached from the Argonaut-Colchuck col), the six-row pitch_detail, descent_text ('reverse the East Ridge') and rappel_detail[1] (the 'snow ledge toward the east gully' belongs to the Northeast Couloir/East Gully).
The row id says east_ridge but the climb is the Southeast Ridge; an id rename is out of scope here.

results.resolution: keep_as_A (adjusted): keep the Hozomeen Lake / 6,800 ft saddle line; rewrite beta, set gain/loss 6,300 and one-way dist_km 9.7, fix itinerary.cal's landing, and drop the Southeast Buttress crux pin; the other pins go to follow-up
results.summary: The page stays the standard South Peak climb from the Hozomeen campground by way of Hozomeen Lake. Its description, gain and distance now match that line, and the map pin marking the neighbouring Southeast Buttress crux was removed.
results.evidence: An independent ascent from the Hozomeen Lake trailhead at the campground leaves the trail after ~1.5 mi at 2,400 ft, crosses Hozomeen Creek, passes a slab wall at 5,800 ft to the 6,800 ft saddle camp, and climbs a 15 ft 5.6 wall on a slanted ledge with Class 3-4 ground and a chimney finish, rappelling at the crux and at an overhang. It is 12 mi round trip from 1,720 to 8,003 ft (~6,300 ft gain). A second South Peak ascent from the same campground by a west-gully line also reports a 5.6 crux bulge near the summit and rappels (15 mi, 7,500 ft). The row's own itinerary already totals 12 mi and 6,300 ft. The app doubles dist_km for the round trip, so 6 mi one way is 9.7 km. The remaining Lightning Creek/Willow Lake pins were kept, since the row documents that as its third approach variant.

ops.find: The Southeast Face offers a third-class approach to the summit, though grading varies by route variant and seasonal conditions. Most parties traverse the northeast ridge where it transitions to mixed terrain. Previous climbing experience on exposed, loose rock is essential.
ops.replace: Mostly Class 3-4 scrambling on loose, fractured rock above the 6,800 ft saddle camp: slabs and connecting gullies lead up the south side to a slanted ledge below the summit, where a short, exposed wall of about 15 ft at roughly 5.6 is the crux, followed by a chimney finish. Most parties rappel the crux on the way down. Previous climbing experience on exposed, loose rock is essential.

results.resolution: do not rewrite the itinerary to Fisher Creek; the high traverse from Easy Pass is the better-documented approach for this line. Only dist_km corrected (24.1 -> 12.1 one way); the approach choice is left for an owner decision
results.summary: Most ascents of this line traverse high from Easy Pass rather than dropping into Fisher Creek, so the trip plan was not rewritten. Only the distance was fixed: the round trip had been stored in a one-way field.
results.evidence: Three independent ascents reach Mesahchie's summit gullies by traversing west from Easy Pass without dropping to Fisher Creek. One goes along the crest over Cub Peak to the 8,050 ft flat spot and the beige south-side gully with the chockstone and rap-sling bench, which is exactly the row's baseFinding and beta. One sidehills at 6,600-6,800 ft and crosses a waterfall on a bench near 6,500 ft beneath the peak; the row's approach text borrows that waterfall. One bivies at the 8,200 ft Katsuk-Mesahchie col and climbs the west gully, which matches the row's name and its 'from Mesahchie Col' beta. The single Fisher Creek ascent (down to Fisher Camp, a 6,700 ft ridge-step bivy) climbs a different line, the South Rib and south gullies (16 mi, 8,200 ft). So the Fisher Creek approach text and pins are the odd ones out, not the itinerary. Rewriting approach, approach_variants and pins to the traverse means choosing between traverse variants, so it is not done here. Separately, dist_km is one-way (the app doubles it). The row's own approach says ~12 km one way / 24.1 km round trip, and its itinerary says ~15 mi round trip.
pin_followups: Owner decision: the approach, approach_variants and waypoints describe dropping into Fisher Creek (the South Rib ascent's approach). The itinerary, timing, overview, name and summit beta describe the high traverse from Easy Pass. Suggest making the traverse primary and keeping Fisher Creek as a second variant, with pins re-placed to match.
The bivy list no longer carries Wing Lake / Lewis Lake / Rainy Pass entries; nothing to do there.

results.summary: This page and 'Cool Glacier / Gerdine Ridge' are the same climb, so they become one page named 'Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Gerdine Ridge / Cool Glacier)'. It keeps the other page's approach, trip plan and map pins and takes this page's descent and its direct variant over Disappointment Peak.
results.evidence: The club route page for the Disappointment Peak Cleaver follows the North Fork Sauk trail to White Pass, a boot path to a 6,600 ft pass, and the White Chuck Glacier to a col at the Suiattle Glacier edge (7,300 ft). It then goes up the cleaver, off it onto snow near 8,600 ft, on a rising traverse under Disappointment Peak to the 9,100 ft Cool Glacier col, and up the Cool Glacier to the 9,600 ft col and the summit (33 mi RT, 8,200 ft). That is the same line as the Gerdine Ridge/Cool Glacier row's approach, climbing_route and waypoints (Glacier Gap 7,300, Cool Glacier saddle 9,600). Separate guide pages also treat 'Gerdine Ridge/Cool Glacier' and the cleaver as one route, with the direct line over Disappointment Peak as a variant. The surviving row's gain (9,400) matches its own itinerary sum; published totals range 8,200-9,200 ft, so it was left. Its approach and 3-day itinerary were kept instead of the retired row's, because they agree with its own waypoints and partner requirements and match the club description.

ops.name: Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Gerdine Ridge / Cool Glacier)

ops.find: An alternate avoids all glacier travel by climbing directly up the South Ridge to Disappointment Peak (9,755 ft) before descending slightly to the saddle above the Cool Glacier — useful for parties without full glacier gear or climbing very late season.
ops.replace: A variant stays on the nose of the cleaver where the standard line steps onto the glacier near 8,500-8,600 ft, following a climbers' path when melted out up mostly Class 3-4 ground with a few low fifth-class moves over Disappointment Peak (9,755 ft), then drops about 150 ft to the saddle above the Cool Glacier to rejoin the standard route. It avoids most of the glacier travel and crevasse hazard in exchange for sustained loose, rockfall-prone scrambling.

ops.expect: Reverse the glacier and ridge to camp.
ops.value: No rappelling; reverse the ascent line on foot. From the summit, descend the ridge to the 9,600 ft col, then down the Cool Glacier to the 9,100 ft col. On the traverse back beneath Disappointment Peak, keep lower and farther from the face than on the way in to cut the time spent under its rockfall. Crevasses on the Cool Glacier open wider as summer goes on and snow bridges weaken, so stay roped and probe suspect bridges. From Glacier Gap, return across the White Chuck basin to White Pass and out the North Fork Sauk River Trail.
